deep.reconstruction:
The page has no derivation and no formulas. It is a verbatim excerpt, with ellipses, from the opening section ('Considérations générales', p. 1) of A.-L. Cauchy's 'Mémoire sur la dispersion de la lumière' (Prague, 1836; Nouveaux exercices de mathématiques). It was copied as reading notes into Riemann's natural-philosophy papers.

Content of the excerpt, in modern terms:
(a) In an earlier memoir (Exercices de mathématiques, vol. V) Cauchy derived the laws of propagation and polarization of light from linear PDEs of elasticity type, the equations of motion of the ether. These have the form d^2 u/dt^2 = (constant-coefficient second-order operator) u. Plane waves u = A exp(i(k.x - w t)) then give a dispersion relation that is homogeneous of degree 2: w^2 = c^2 |k|^2 (direction-dependent in crystals).
(b) The prism shows that in transparent bodies the phase velocity w/k depends on colour.
(c) Wave theorists hold that colour is fixed by the period T = 2*pi/w of the ether vibrations.
(d) Hence there should be a relation v = v(T). The truncated second-order PDEs (equations (11), Exerc. vol. IV, p. 131) cannot give such a relation, because they make v independent of T.
(e) Those PDEs were themselves obtained from more general formulas (Exerc. vol. III, p. 190 ff.). These are the lattice sums for a system of point molecules with central forces.
(f) Coriolis suggested that the terms dropped in that reduction might explain dispersion.

What follows in Cauchy's memoir, not on this page: he keeps the higher-order terms of the expansion in powers of k times the molecular spacing a. This gives w^2 = c^2 k^2 (1 + b1 k^2 + b2 k^4 + ...). Hence the refractive index has the form n = A + B/lambda^2 + C/lambda^4 + ..., Cauchy's dispersion formula.

The page itself only states the motivation. Riemann (or whoever copied it) adds nothing of his own.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics on the page.
Minor copying features are visible: 'naturelle' for Cauchy's 'naturel', and '&' or 'est' ambiguity in 'chaque couleur est déterminée'.

results.what: Statement that dispersion requires frequency-dependent phase velocity, which second-order homogeneous elastic-ether PDEs cannot supply; proposal (credited to Coriolis) to retain neglected higher-order molecular terms.
results.modern_name: Spatial dispersion from discrete lattice (nonlocal) effects; Cauchy's dispersion theory / Cauchy dispersion formula n = A + B/lambda^2 + ...
results.usually_credited_to: A.-L. Cauchy (1830s, Mémoire sur la dispersion de la lumière, 1836), idea suggested by G. Coriolis

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reading excerpt copied from Cauchy's well-known 1836 dispersion memoir. It contains no original content by Riemann. It only documents that he read Cauchy on the ether and dispersion, which fits his known interest in natural philosophy and ether theory.

checkable.asserts: Illustration only, not on the page. For a discrete 1D lattice, w = 2*sqrt(K/m)*sin(k*a/2) expands as a*sqrt(K/m)*k*(1 - a**2*k**2/24 + ...). So retaining terms beyond the continuum limit makes the phase velocity w/k depend on k, which is Cauchy's mechanism for dispersion.

In the continuum (truncated second-order PDE) limit w = c*k, the phase velocity is constant (derivative 0), so there is no dispersion. This is the claim in the excerpt that equations (11) cannot yield a v(T) relation.

transcription_corrections: '(11) p. 131 [?] 2. Vol 4. Exerc. d. Math.' reads more plausibly as '(11) p. 131 du Vol. 4e Exerc. d. Math.' or similar; the '2' is likely 'du' or 'd.'.
'la nature de chaque couleur & déterminée' should be 'la nature de chaque couleur est déterminée' (Cauchy's text). The manuscript sign is an abbreviated 'est' or a slip.
'Il est donc naturelle' matches the manuscript; Cauchy's original has 'naturel'.
In 'la vitesse de propagation de la lumière' (line 8) the manuscript shows a struck or overwritten 'la' ('de l[a] la lumière').
Heading: 'Cauchy. Mém. sur la dispersion p. 1. Considérations générales.' The reading is fine; 'Cauchy' is underlined.
